### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/setup`, `@objectstack/studio`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/book.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/book.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `requiredPermissions (literal, 42 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **184** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f5afa82e7851602d2a7f6de20f72a0889b445301` — the merge of head `9d4b627c971081e8acbb07a2fd76340a54bef87c` into base `87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f5afa82e7851602d2a7f6de20f72a0889b445301 && git checkout f5afa82e7851602d2a7f6de20f72a0889b445301
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a 9d4b627c971081e8acbb07a2fd76340a54bef87c && git checkout -B drift-repro 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a && git merge --no-ff 9d4b627c971081e8acbb07a2fd76340a54bef87c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `899b3e2f7cd924e3a6de98b481f3a9dc6f4b00b8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/book.zod.ts + packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-docs.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-capability-references.ts, packages/apps/setup/src/setup-manual.book.ts, packages/apps/studio/src/studio-manual.book.ts

Inputs read: card #36029 (body and all six comments, ruling 7122770897 included), PR #37591 (body, 25 files, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on the head: every one is `success` or `skipped`, none failed. Code outside the diff was read in the tree at the head, never reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- `BookAudienceSchema` accepts a fourth arm, `{ systemPermission: string }`, strict. A widening: the shape was refused before. No value that parsed before parses differently now (the three older arms are untouched, and they are tried first). Right.
- `BookAudience` (the exported type) gains a union member. A consumer that narrowed with `typeof audience === 'object'` and then read `.permissionSet` stops compiling; the one in-repo reader (`BookPreview.tsx`) is fixed in this diff, and `audienceAllows` narrows by key. Right at `minor` under `Metadata-protocol: added`; the changeset does not tell a TypeScript consumer (see N2).
- `AudienceCaller.systemPermissions` is a new optional field, and `audienceAllows` reads it for the new arm only. The `public`, `org` and `{ permissionSet }` answers are the same predicates as on `main`. Absent or not a list denies. Right.
- `@objectstack/rest`: an optional port (`resolveAudienceSystemPermissions`), an optional option (`needSystemPermissions`), an optional result field, and `anySystemPermissionAudience`. All additive. A `{ systemPermission }` book takes every docs door off the fast path, which the arm needs. Right.
- `@objectstack/runtime`: on a delegated envelope the MCP docs door reads the delegating person's capabilities in place of the envelope's list, never a union. The same holder its `{ permissionSet }` reading already uses on `main`. Right (wording: N1).
- `@objectstack/lint`: `capability-reference-unknown` gains one position, `books[i].audience.systemPermission`, as a warning. Existing messages are unchanged (the new `key` parameter defaults to the old word). Right.
- `@objectstack/setup`, `@objectstack/studio`: each ships a gated manual, so `setup_overview` and `studio_overview` go from `org` to capability-gated on every docs door. This is the narrowing the ruling asked for. Right for those two docs.
- The same two manuals also change the effective audience of docs that are not theirs. Not declared, and wrong: S1.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` stand on the PR body and in the changeset, and they agree with the diff: a new accepted audience value, nothing removed or tightened in the schema. `added` takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves, and the changeset gives `minor` to all eight (`spec`, `rest`, `runtime`, `lint`, `setup`, `studio`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n`). `Check Changeset` is green. The level is right.

Two sentences of the changeset body do not hold as written: "Nothing to migrate: no stored or authored value changes meaning" (S1), and "a key beside `systemPermission` is refused at parse" (N2).

### ③ Boundary flags

- os-dev report 7112446659, open question A to D: answered by the maintainer ruling relayed in 7122770897 (A). This diff implements A.
- The ruling's relay names `resolvePermissionSetsForContext` as the source of the holdings. On REST the diff reads the caller's own `systemPermissions` instead, and says so in the PR body. Judged right: that list is the one `callerSystemPermissions` hands `holdsRequiredPermissions` for the app arm, so the manual and its app are decided by one list with no second resolution to drift; the maintainer's own words rule the outcome ("every admin who can open Setup can read it"), which this meets. Not escalated.
- Arm name left to the spec lane: `systemPermission`. Right: it is the grant side's word (`systemPermissions`), and the lint and `os explain` already speak it.
- ADR-0046 §6.7 note: split out by claim 7194108111 into a seat-run Tier H PR. It is not in this diff and no such PR was open at review time. The jsdoc here already cites §6.7 for the arm, so the card stays open on that note.
- PR-body acceptance notes: the Console address and label changes are the lane seat's; the two-key parse is N2; the comment drift in `packages/apps/setup/src/index.ts` is carried from the earlier report and left as noted.
- SQL push-down: nothing new. REST reads the list off the resolved caller, with no query. The MCP door reuses the one memoised grant resolution its `{ permissionSet }` reading already makes (`holdings ??=`), so a gate that reads both forms still resolves the person once. No new id materialisation, no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/book.zod.ts`** (hits), against ruling 7122770897 and its first consumers.

The arm is what the ruling asked for: one key, a string, strict, described. `audienceAllows` tries the forms in the order the union parses them, and an unrecognised shape still denies. Tried and held:

- Anonymous: `authenticated` is false before either gated form is read, so a list on an unauthenticated caller opens nothing (pinned in `book.test.ts`, and as 401 on REST).
- Missing or non-array list: `undefined`, `null` and a bare string all deny, in the spec helper and again in `resolveAudienceCaller` (pinned on both).
- Name collision with a permission set: the two forms read two separate lists, so a set named like the token opens nothing, and a capability named like a set opens no `{ permissionSet }` book (pinned both ways, and on the MCP door).
- Delegated OAuth: the person's own capabilities decide, with no union with the envelope (pinned, including an envelope that carries the capability the person lacks).

S1 (should-fix) — the two manuals claim docs that are not their package's. `SETUP_MANUAL_BOOK` and `STUDIO_MANUAL_BOOK` use `groups: [{ include: '*' }]`, scoped by the book's own package. `matchesInclude` drops a doc from a scoped rule only when the doc carries a `packageId` that differs; a doc with no stamped package is in every scope (pinned on `main`: `book.test.ts`, "a doc with no stamped `packageId` is in every scope"). A stored doc row bound to no package is served with no `_packageId` (`withRowBinding`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-bindings.ts`), and `docCorpusOf` reads that stamp alone. So wherever either package is installed, every package-less doc is claimed by `setup_manual` and `studio_manual`, and its effective audience (the §6.7 union) stops being the `org` fallback. A member who read such a doc before this change gets 403 on its read and loses it from the list, the content answer and the MCP search; the doc also shows up inside the Setup and Studio manual trees. The card does not ask for this, the PR does not declare it, and three sentences in the diff say otherwise: the book files' "over this package's own docs", the new spec test's "`include: '*'` reaches only the book's own package" (its corpus is all stamped), and the changeset's "no stored or authored value changes meaning". Graded should-fix, not must-fix, because the package-less state is ADR-0070's legacy and migration-source state, and because this was read in the tree, not measured on a boot. The fix is inside the diff: have each manual claim by its own namespace (`setup_*`, `studio_*`) or by pinned pages, correct the three sentences, and pin the control: with both manuals registered, a doc carrying no `_packageId` that no other book claims stays readable by a member on the list, the single read and the MCP answer.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract; left as accepted deviations or a follow-up card):

- N1 — the jsdoc on `BookAudienceSchema` ("the same answer an app's `requiredPermissions: [token]` gets") and on `AudienceCaller.systemPermissions` ("exactly for whoever can open an app gated on that token") is true of a session. On the MCP door's delegated envelope the person's capabilities decide whatever list the envelope carries, by design and as the runtime docblock says. The spec sentences could name that exception.
- N2 — an audience carrying both keys parses as the `{ permissionSet }` arm with `systemPermission` dropped, because the older arm is not strict (the PR body says so). The changeset's "a key beside `systemPermission` is refused at parse" is therefore not true of `permissionSet`, and the type accepts the two-key literal. Worth a follow-up card: a lint finding on the two-key shape, or a strict older arm under its own narrowing declaration. The changeset could also tell a TypeScript consumer to narrow `BookAudience` by key.
- N3 — with a gated manual shipped by two platform packages, `allReadable` is false in every deployment that installs either one, so the docs doors' fast path no longer applies there: each doc read, doc list and app-nav doc gate now reads the doc corpus and runs the audience pass. Correct, and the price of the ruling; worth a line in the PR body, and a follow-up if the docs doors show up in a profile.

**Implementing files, sentence by sentence.**

- `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts` — agrees. Holdings are read only when a `{ systemPermission }` book is among the books judged; a rejecting or non-list answer leaves the field off and the audience denies; permission sets are not resolved for a capability-only gate (pinned); the port, when present, replaces the caller's list.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-docs.ts` — agrees. The port exists only on a delegated envelope; an unknown person, a person with no membership in the request's organization, or unreadable grants throw and read as closed; one resolution per gate.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-capability-references.ts` — agrees with its header and with `os explain`.
- `packages/apps/setup/src/setup-manual.book.ts`, `packages/apps/studio/src/studio-manual.book.ts` — the audience is the token each app's `requiredPermissions` names, and the dogfood pin shows the member and the administrator on a real boot. The membership sentence does not hold: S1.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-a4oj04`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `99447c4346f0c6dfb7779ca26d2e2c784a858afb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/book.zod.ts + packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-docs.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-capability-references.ts, packages/apps/setup/src/setup-manual.book.ts, packages/apps/studio/src/studio-manual.book.ts

DELTA review from `899b3e2f7cd924e3a6de98b481f3a9dc6f4b00b8` (record 7196156631: PASS, should-fix S1, nits N1 to N3) to this head.

Inputs read: card #36029 (body and all six comments, ruling 7122770897 included), PR #37591 (the body as it stands on this head, its 25 files, the net diff against `main`, and the one-commit delta between the two heads in full), record 7196156631, and the check-runs on the head, read at 2026-11-26T16:38Z: every one is `success` or `skipped`, the re-run `Test Core (5/10)` and the second `Check Changeset` run included. Code outside the diff was read in the tree at the head, never reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- The delta changes no schema, no type and no function body. In `book.zod.ts` two docblocks move and nothing else. The accept-set and the public surface are the ones record 7196156631 judged: the fourth, strict `{ systemPermission }` arm (a widening), `AudienceCaller.systemPermissions`, the optional port, option and export on `@objectstack/rest`, the delegated reading on the MCP docs door, and the one new lint position. All unchanged, all still right.
- The two manuals' membership rule changes from `include: '*'` to `include: 'setup_*'` and `include: 'studio_*'`. Derived from the tree: the docs whose effective audience this PR moves are now the docs named under one of the two prefixes that carry the manual's package or no package. On this tree that is `setup_overview` and `studio_overview`, the two the ruling names. A doc bound to no package and named outside the prefixes keeps the `org` fallback. Declared in the changeset and in the PR body. Right.
- Nothing else is implied by the delta: its other six files are three test files, the changeset, one docs page and `book.zod.ts` with the two docblocks above.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` stand on the PR body and in the changeset, and the changeset gives `minor` to the same eight packages. `Check Changeset` is green on both of its runs on this head.

The two changeset sentences the earlier record named now hold. The strict-arm sentence states the parse as the tree does it: `{ systemPermission, label }` is refused, and an object that also carries `permissionSet` is taken by the older, non-strict arm with the other key dropped. "Nothing to migrate" is now bounded to what the manuals claim ("Only docs named under those prefixes change audience"). The changeset also tells a TypeScript consumer to narrow `BookAudience` by key.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Record 7196156631, S1: answered on this head; judged under ④.
- Record 7196156631, N1 to N3: all three touched (the two spec docblocks, the changeset, the PR body); judged under ④.
- os-dev report 7112446659 (open question A to D), the holdings source on REST and the arm name: answered as the earlier record has them. Nothing in the delta touches them.
- ADR-0046 §6.7 note: still not in this diff, and no other open PR names the card. Claim 7194108111 keeps the card open until both have merged.
- The PR body against the tree. Its readings of this head match: the namespace claim in both book files; the three pins with their catch-all controls (spec, REST, MCP); the case counts of the five suites (50, 22, 14, 28 and 3 cases stand in the files); the two-doc inventory; no file naming the old Console address; the fast-path note; the two-key parse. Two readings do not match, and both are nits: N5 and N6.
- SQL push-down: the delta adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/book.zod.ts`** (hits). The delta here is prose: the docblock on `BookAudienceSchema` now says the app equivalence holds in a session and names the delegated exception, and the docblock on `AudienceCaller.systemPermissions` says which transport fills the list with another person's capabilities. Both agree with `packageDocsReadGate` at this head. The claim rule the fix leans on was re-read in the same file and is untouched: `matchesInclude` drops a doc from a scoped rule only when the doc is stamped with another package, the glob is anchored on the whole name, and `resolveDocAudiences` falls back to `org` for a doc no book claims.

- **S1: closed.** Both manuals now claim by their package's doc namespace, which is the package's own identity for docs under ADR-0046 §3.2, and the three sentences the earlier record named are corrected (both book files, the spec test's comment, the changeset). The control it asked for is pinned at three levels, each beside a catch-all control that shows the pin can go red: `book.test.ts` (an unstamped doc keeps `org`), the REST suite with both manuals registered (a member lists it with and without content and reads it), and the MCP suite (found and read).

Tried against the fix, and held:

- A doc stamped with another package and named `setup_…` is not claimed: the package scope still applies under the glob.
- A doc bound to no package and named under one of the two prefixes is still claimed. The changeset says so, and the prefix belongs to that package's namespace. Accepted.
- A doc bound to no package that no book claims is still listed under *Uncategorized* in each manual's tree, to a reader of that manual. That is the orphan rule on `main`, outside the diff, and the same doc the package's implicit book listed before this change. No audience moves.

No must-fix. No should-fix. Three new nits.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract at this head; left as accepted deviations or a follow-up card, since a fix outside the prose faces moves the head):

- **N1** — touched; the exception is now named. One residue: the `BookAudienceSchema` sentence reads as if it held on every door, and it describes the MCP docs door, the one transport that hands in the person's holdings. The `AudienceCaller` sentence beside it names that door. Accepted as written.
- **N2** — the changeset sentences now hold, and the TypeScript note is there. The follow-up it suggested (a lint finding on the two-key shape, or a strict older arm under its own narrowing declaration) is still only a suggestion.
- **N3** — the PR body now carries the fast-path line under its acceptance notes.
- **N4** — new. Each manual's membership now rests on the doc-name prefix. ADR-0046 §3.2 requires the prefix, but the lint that enforces it (`docs/namespace-prefix`) runs in `os build`, and these two packages are built by tsup with no suite of their own. The new pins also exercise fixture copies of the manuals: the shipped Setup constant is read only by the dogfood boot, for `setup_overview`, and no pin reads the shipped Studio constant. Worth a follow-up card: one pin over `SETUP_MANUAL_BOOK` and `STUDIO_MANUAL_BOOK` themselves, that every doc the package registers is claimed by its manual. It would hold the membership sentence in both book files.
- **N5** — new. `packages/spec/liveness/book.json`: the `audience` row's evidence and note were rewritten for the new arm, but its `verifiedAt` did not move; the date that moved is on the `name` row, whose evidence the diff does not touch. The PR body says the `audience` row was re-verified. Age is a worklist, never a gate, so nothing reads wrong; the next re-verification of the row can set it.
- **N6** — new, on the PR body (a prose face, so the seat can correct it without moving the head). The ablation totals are the earlier head's (12 and 26 cases) under a heading that says every run was on this head, where the same suites hold 14 and 28. The S1 pins carry in-suite controls in place of an ablation; the body could say so.

**Implementing files, sentence by sentence.**

- `packages/apps/setup/src/setup-manual.book.ts`, `packages/apps/studio/src/studio-manual.book.ts` — agree now. The audience is the token each app's `requiredPermissions` names, the `include` is the namespace each package's manifest header declares, and the sentence on why not `'*'` is the rule `matchesInclude` implements. The condition "under that prefix" is stated; see N4 for what holds it.
- `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-docs.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-capability-references.ts` — not touched by the delta; re-read at this head and they agree with the contract as the earlier record found. Their suites gained the S1 pins named above.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-a4oj04`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [45861150445](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/45861150445) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Test Core (2/10)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/45861150445/job/140053536000)** — 失败步骤: Run this shard's tests
